producer: backend/app/utils/clock_bridge.py (_Markers), on the clock bridge's existing dedicated asyncpg connection

enable.dark_unless: a trace in the pid is ARMED (the bridge is running) AND CLOCK_MARKER_CASE matches case_pattern AND wall_now < CLOCK_MARKER_EXPIRES_AT <= wall_now + arm_max_s

channels.addressing: one request channel per producer incarnation and run; the collector learns it from that run's bind message on the reply channel

clock.domain: time.monotonic of the producer pid (CLOCK_MONOTONIC; the same callable the Kalshi/PM/nonvenue/fold traces use for *_mono)
clock.rounding: lo and hi are rounded to 6 decimals; q is the quantum to expand each by before claiming strict order
clock.lo: read first in the notification callback, which asyncpg schedules with call_soon after the notification left the socket: receipt <= lo
clock.hi: read immediately before the reply's pg_notify is sent: hi <= reply send
clock.use: a producer stamp P with P > lo + q came after the request was received (so after collector S); P < hi - q came before the reply was sent (so before collector R). Equal or overlapping stamps prove no strict order.

accept_rules: size checked before any parse: 0 < bytes <= 256 else fault big
malformed JSON, missing/extra keys or bad types: fault bad
case/tok/run not this run's: fault foreign
slot or nonce already seen this run: fault dup
slot <= last accepted slot: fault ord
more than queue requests waiting: fault q
no retry, no catch-up: a dropped slot is a gap

fields.rx: notification ordinal in this run, valid or not (1-based)

bind.when: once per LISTEN, after the run's first P probe on that connection; listen counts LISTENs this run (a P reconnect re-LISTENs while markers are not halted)

not_in_scope: no marker log line; P's 256-line cap is untouched
wire bytes are an ESTIMATE from payload plus fixed framing, not a wire measurement
no collector side here; one collector PG session is unadmitted
